title: Precessional knowledge encoded in myth
statement: A recurring family of world myths — the great mill that turns, is unhinged, and is wrecked; the axle askew; the ages that grind on and break — encodes observational knowledge of the precession of the equinoxes in narrative form, carried by tellers who no longer understood the technical content (the Hamlet's Mill thesis); the corpus adopts a bounded version of this reading as the mythological layer of its precessional chronology.

includes: The bounded encoding reading: the mill/axle family and cognate age-structure motifs read as carrying precessional content, at the strength the published Explainer states it
The canonical resonance layer: the canon's cycle symbolism (the emblem as 'infinity in time'; the cycle sign) read alongside the encoding thesis without being fused with it
The relationship to the chronology: this record supplies the mythological layer that woh-claim-0003 references; the astronomy and the age-lattice live in 0003, not here
excludes: The Doubled Signature principle — the corpus's extension beyond Hamlet's Mill — reserved as its own future claim with a speculative label
Santillana and Dechend's specific etymologies and identifications taken severally; the record adopts the thesis's shape, not its every instance
Any claim that precession was measured to modern precision in prehistory; encoded observation is not stated precision
Dating claims; all dating belongs to woh-claim-0003
The contested ancient-knowledge thesis as settled; the record inherits 0003's 'contested' marking of that layer

source_references.locator: The whole-work thesis; the mill/axle motif family assembled across traditions. Access remains metadata_only pending inspection — the wantlist carries it, and the published Explainer is the project's close engagement to date
TBWTT-3:305 (the emblem as infinity in time, 'the most ancient symbol'); TBWTT-5:7 (the Gate of the Fish material the Explainer reads)
ETTMTTP-2:24 (the cycle sign 'found in numerous ancient writings')
Journal for the History of Astronomy 3 (1972), pp. 206-211 — the standard scholarly demolition of Hamlet's Mill's method

alternatives.statement: Hamlet's Mill's method is unsound — motif-hunting without controls — and the mill family carries no astronomical content (the mainstream review position).
Mill, axle, and turning-sky imagery are agricultural and cosmological symbolism natural to any grain-processing, star-watching culture; no encoded measurement is needed.
Some late traditions encode precession after its Hellenistic discovery; the deep-prehistory extension is unsupported.

revision_triggers: Claim woh-claim-0003 is revised or retired.
Inspection of Hamlet's Mill (currently metadata_only) materially changes what the thesis actually claims or how the Explainer represents it.
The motif family fails a controlled comparative test, vindicating the method-failure alternative.
Public prose begins asserting prehistoric measurement precision or Doubled Signature content, which this record excludes.
